title: Safe QR privacy-safe quishing case
description: Proposed schema, not a claim that the $id is deployed. Store only public, source-supported facts and fraud infrastructure. Never store names, handles, profile URLs, photos, raw posts, QR images, victim account numbers or other personal data about posters/victims, including inside summaries, evidence, URLs or hashes. Schema validation cannot detect personal data inside strings; semantic redaction and a publication gate are mandatory. Do not publish cases or indicators solely because they validate.

id.description: Set by pipeline, not LLM: sqr_ + SHA-256 of canonical sourceUrl + newline + stable within-source case key assigned by pipeline. Store/upsert same source-case ID on later scans. Cross-source campaign merging requires corroborated shared infrastructure/context; identical lure alone is insufficient. Never hash poster/victim identifiers.

recordKind.description: A hypothetical warning or demonstration must not be presented as a real victim incident.

lure.description: Neutral privacy-safe description, e.g. payment for parking. No names, unique victim details, or unsupported attribution.

channel.description: Where the QR appeared; SMS-link phishing with no evidenced QR is not automatically a quishing case. Explain physical placement, e.g. parking meter/EV charger/table, in lure.

payloadType.description: Actual decoded or explicitly source-described QR payload, not a guess from the lure. A payment lure may encode a URL rather than SPD.

indicators.description: May be empty. Extract only values the cited source explicitly associates with fraudulent use. Ordinary bank/city/operator domains or helpdesk phone numbers mentioned as legitimate advice are not malicious indicators. Broad bank-code and account patterns must never be used alone for blocking.

countryCode.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 if sourced, otherwise null.

location.description: Geography of reported campaign/placement only. No street address, GPS, home/workplace or individual victim location; use null if unknown.

firstSeen.description: Earliest explicitly evidenced occurrence date at known day precision. Not article publication or ingestion date. Null if only publication date, month or year is known; preserve qualified timing in evidenceNote.

anyOf.description: Canonical public incident article or official warning URL. Never a victim/poster profile URL; remove tracking and personal identifiers. Do not replace evidence with a homepage.

firstSeenSourceUrl.description: Incident source supporting firstSeen; null when firstSeen is null.

sourceUrl.description: Canonical public incident article or official warning URL. Never a victim/poster profile URL; remove tracking and personal identifiers. Do not replace evidence with a homepage.

sourcePublishedDate.description: Publication date of main source if explicitly available; never substitute occurrence date or crawl date.

summaryCs.description: Short neutral Czech summary. State uncertainty and distinguish a warning/simulation from a real incident. No poster/victim personal data.

summaryEn.description: Equivalent short neutral English summary with the same uncertainty and privacy restrictions.

confidence.description: Evidence strength, not an LLM probability: high=explicit primary-source confirmation/observation; medium=credible sourced report; low=unverified or ambiguous. Repetition of one report is not corroboration.

evidenceNote.description: Privacy-safe paraphrase explaining evidence, uncertainty, approximate timing and missing facts. No copied personal data or unsourced accusations.

firstSeenSourceUrl.description: Canonical public incident article or official warning URL. Never a victim/poster profile URL; remove tracking and personal identifiers. Do not replace evidence with a homepage.

value.description: Source-supported fraud infrastructure only, normalized without adding missing digits/characters. Domain=lowercase ASCII/Punycode; IBAN=uppercase no spaces. Patterns use literal * placeholders (not executable regex). Strip victim names, emails, tokens and query identifiers. Never include ordinary legitimate infrastructure as malicious.

network.description: For crypto_address only: source-supported chain/network; omit if unknown.

sourceUrl.description: Canonical public incident article or official warning URL. Never a victim/poster profile URL; remove tracking and personal identifiers. Do not replace evidence with a homepage.

evidence.description: Privacy-safe paraphrase of source statement associating this exact value/pattern with fraud; appearance somewhere on page is insufficient. Do not invent a quote.

confidence.description: Evidence strength, not an LLM probability: high=explicit primary-source confirmation/observation; medium=credible sourced report; low=unverified or ambiguous. Repetition of one report is not corroboration.
